Issue 1

⚔️ US-Iran Full-Scale Escalation: Tanker Bombing, Missile Attack on US Warships, Retaliatory Strikes on Jordan and Bahrain

Key summary
  • The US carried out airstrikes destroying 5 Iranian oil tankers (CENTCOM released video), announced as a response to the IRGC's two separate ballistic missile attacks on US Navy warships over two days. The IRGC claimed it struck two cruise-missile/Aegis-equipped destroyers (DDG-119, DDG-53), 8 tankers, and 10 vessels in the Persian Gulf.
  • The IRGC announced it launched missiles targeting US forces at the Al Azraq base in Jordan as a retaliatory measure, and footage captured Jordan's air defense intercepting Iranian missiles.

🛢️ International Oil Prices Surge (Brent Nears $100)·US Stock Market Plunge

Key summary
  • Amid the US-Iran escalation, international oil prices surged to near $100 per barrel. Asian stock markets contracted while US stock markets fell amid soaring oil prices and Treasury yields.
  • The Iranian government urged citizens to cut consumption following another domestic fuel price hike, coinciding with an economic contraction phase driven by intensified US sanctions on sectors including Iran's aviation industry. The US announced new sanctions targeting Iran's aviation sector, further tightening economic pressure.

Issue 3

🚢 Sharp Drop in Strait of Hormuz Transit Volume·Logistics Crisis in the South, South Korean Government Considers Sending On-Site Investigation Team

Key summary
  • The number of vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz has fallen below the recent 10-day average; according to preliminary Kpler data, Tuesday's commercial vessel transits numbered 6, down from 9 the previous day.
  • The South Korean government is dispatching an on-site investigation team to the Middle East and reviewing whether to support troop deployment to the Strait of Hormuz, though it denies receiving a specific November deadline request from the US side. South Korea's Ministry of National Defense stated it will send an on-site investigation team to the Hormuz region.

🕊️ Qatar Continues Mediation Between US and Iran, Urges Halt to Escalation

Key summary
  • Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met in Beijing with Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, stating that 'pressure by force is not a solution' and urging dialogue and negotiation (September 8, Beijing).

  • Qatar welcomed the UK's import ban on goods from Israeli settlements, calling it 'an important measure to deter occupation.'

This page automatically collects and summarizes public news coverage and material from relevant institutions across Qatar, Iran, other major countries and Korea. News is gathered by querying Google News RSS feeds, Naver News search, and outlet RSS (Al Jazeera, BBC, etc.) with keywords such as Qatar, the Middle East and energy; in-depth reports are collected directly from the publication boards and RSS of domestic and international research institutes, international organizations and consultancies (supplemented by news search targeting those publishers), keeping only analyses and reports on the Middle East situation, the Iran war and their industrial, supply-chain and energy repercussions. The report list accumulates items published since the war's outbreak (2026-02-28), split into domestic and overseas and ordered by publication date (newest first). Collection and summarization rely on each outlet's publicly available headline and snippet; for subscription or paywalled outlets, the full article can be opened through the provided source link only after the reader signs in or subscribes to that outlet directly. The collected articles are automatically clustered and summarized by issue, and translated into English and Arabic, by Anthropic Claude (Sonnet 5) AI. The whole process runs and publishes automatically twice a day (07:00 and 15:30 Qatar time) via GitHub Actions. The Qatar government activity section separately curates only official statements, announcements and actions on the war and regional situation by Qatar government and state entities — the Emir, the Prime Minister, the ministries of Foreign Affairs, Defense and Interior, the Government Communications Office (GCO), QatarEnergy and the state news agency (QNA). Owing to automated collection some articles or reports may be missed, so please re-verify important issues against the original sources and further searches.
- Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Qatar, Commercial Section · KOTRA Doha
